basis: Trichomonas infection directly inflames the glans and foreskin, including preputial skin.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: balanoposthitis directly affects genital skin; the exclusion of purely reproductive organs does not exclude foreskin inflammation.

basis: DCX-related cortical malformation defines the disease. Contractures occur in 30-79% but reflect neurologic motor impairment rather than direct skeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: flexion contractures occur in 30-79%, but are secondary to cerebral motor dysfunction; direct musculoskeletal pathology is not established.

basis: Craniofacial dysostosis defines the disease; structural eyelid ptosis occurs in 80-99%. Sinus hypoplasia in 80-99% does not establish respiratory dysfunction.

decisions.pulmonary: none: absent or hypoplastic sinuses occur in 80-99%, but this anatomical finding alone does not establish impaired airway or sinus function.

basis: Definition includes neurodevelopmental disease, frequent limb malformations and lymphopenia. Lymphatic vessels lack an axis; lymphopenia alone does not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.haematologic: primary: frequent lymphopenia is an explicit defining blood-cell abnormality, even when caused by altered trafficking rather than cell destruction.
decisions.cardiovascular: none: lymphatic vessels are outside the specified cardiovascular axis; no heart or blood-vessel disease is established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: craniofacial and limb malformations are explicitly included as frequent structural manifestations in the disease definition.

basis: Severe congenital CNS malformation defines disease. Amyotrophy in 2/2 accompanies profound motor impairment; scalp folds in 2/2 do not establish skin dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: amyotrophy in 2/2 accompanies severe spastic tetraplegia; evidence does not establish direct muscle disease rather than secondary wasting.

basis: Cloverleaf skull and generalized skeletal dysplasia define disease. Pulmonary hypoplasia is usual (>30%) in the parent thanatophoric dysplasia phenotype.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia is usual (>30%) in thanatophoric dysplasia, the supplied parent; this represents lung underdevelopment with functional loss.

basis: Monoclonal cryoproteins cause occlusive vasculopathy; acral ulcers and peripheral neuropathy each occur in 30-79%. Renal disease is 5-29%; type I is not inherently autoimmune.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: characteristic small-vessel occlusion by precipitated cryoproteins is a vascular disease process, distinct from true vasculitis reported in 5-29%.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: monoclonal protein precipitation is not inherently autoimmune or immune-complex disease; an associated lymphoma is a separate diagnosis.

basis: Brainstem tract maldevelopment, permanent horizontal gaze dysfunction and progressive scoliosis define the syndrome. Hearing impairment occurs in only 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: primary: permanent loss of conjugate horizontal eye movements is a defining diagnostic feature; ocular involvement is therefore primary.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines disease. Joint hypermobility in 5/16 (~31%) lacks demonstrated damage or functional loss; hearing impairment in 4/17 is below 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint hypermobility in 5/16 (~31%) meets frequency alone; joint damage, instability causing dysfunction or other direct skeletal injury is not established.

basis: Glycosylation disorder with lethal skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia is usual (>30%) with severe thoracic restriction. Nail changes in 30-79% lack demonstrated dysfunction.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia is usual (>30%) in this lethal thoracic dysplasia; inclusion relies on the usual disease course, beyond narrow-chest morphology alone.
decisions.dermatologic: none: nail hypoplasia and abnormal morphology occur in 30-79%, but do not establish functional nail or skin damage.
